title: Email delivery is a pluggable adapter behind a narrow contract
asA: operator swapping a stub adapter for a real provider or vice versa without touching auth code
iWant: the auth flow to depend on one small interface and know nothing about the provider
soThat: provider migration, test doubles, and outage fallbacks are project decisions instead of blueprint rewrites

acceptanceCriteria.description: The magic-link routes and managers call the email-delivery-adapter through a single send({ to, subject, textBody, htmlBody }) method returning { ok, providerStatus, providerMessageId, error }; no provider-specific fields, credentials, or endpoints appear in the routes or managers.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the auth code path is walked from POST /login to send completion
acceptanceCriteria.when: the outgoing calls to the adapter interface are enumerated
acceptanceCriteria.then: only the declared send method is invoked, with only the declared arguments, and the returned outcome is consumed only via the declared fields

acceptanceCriteria.description: An adapter that returns { ok: false, error } surfaces the failure to the auth event log via an adapterSendFailed entry, but does not change the POST /login response body or status.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a registered principal submits POST /login and the adapter's send resolves with { ok: false, error: 'boom' }
acceptanceCriteria.when: the response and log stream are captured
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response body and status match a successful send exactly, and exactly one adapterSendFailed entry is emitted with the error string in the outcome field

acceptanceCriteria.description: The blueprint ships a stub adapter for testing whose send resolves { ok: true, providerStatus: 200, providerMessageId: 'stub' } and records outgoing calls in memory; the project uses the stub in tests and swaps in the real adapter in production without touching the routes or managers.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the stub adapter is wired into a scratch project's test harness
acceptanceCriteria.when: POST /login runs against a registered principal
acceptanceCriteria.then: the stub's send is invoked with the declared arguments and its in-memory record contains one call with those arguments
